{{Short description|Statistical models in epidemiology}}
'''Marginal structural models''' are a class of [[statistical model]]s used for [[causal inference]] in [[epidemiology]].<ref>{{cite journal|last1=Robins|first1=James|last2=Hernán|first2=Miguel|last3=Brumback|first3=Babette|author3-link= Babette Brumback |title=Marginal Structural Models and Causal Inference in Epidemiology|journal=Epidemiology|date=September 2000|volume=11|issue=5|pages=550–60|url=http://epiresearch.org/wp-content/uploads/2014/07/Robins_EPI_2000_11_550.pdf|doi=10.1097/00001648-200009000-00011|pmid=10955408|citeseerx=10.1.1.116.7039|s2cid=8907527 }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Hernán |first1=Miguel Ángel |last2=Brumback |first2=Babette |last3=Robins |first3=James M. |date=2000 |title=Marginal Structural Models to Estimate the Causal Effect of Zidovudine on the Survival of HIV-Positive Men |journal=Epidemiology |volume=11 |issue=5 |pages=561–570 |doi=10.1097/00001648-200009000-00012 |jstor=3703998 |pmid=10955409 |issn=1044-3983|doi-access=free }}</ref> Such models handle the issue of time-dependent confounding in evaluation of the efficacy of interventions by [[inverse probability weighting]] for receipt of treatment, they allow us to estimate the average causal effects. For instance, in the study of the effect of [[zidovudine]] in [[AIDS]]-related mortality, [[CD4|CD4 lymphocyte]] is used both for treatment indication, is influenced by treatment, and affects survival. Time-dependent confounders are typically highly prognostic of health outcomes and applied in dosing or indication for certain therapies, such as body weight or lab values such as [[alanine aminotransferase]] or [[bilirubin]].{{citation needed|date=May 2023}}

The first marginal structural models were introduced in 2000. The works of [[James Robins]], [[Babette Brumback]], and [[Miguel Hernán]] provided an intuitive theory and an easy-to-implement software which made them popular for the analysis of longitudinal data.<ref>{{cite journal|first1=Tomohiro|last1=Shinozaki|first2=Etsuji|last2=Suzuki|url=https://www.jstage.jst.go.jp/article/jea/30/9/30_JE20200226/_article|format=pdf|title=Understanding Marginal Structural Models for Time-Varying Exposures: Pitfalls and Tips|journal = Journal of Epidemiology|date=September 5, 2020|volume=30|issue=9|pages=377–389|issn=	0917-5040|doi=10.2188/jea.JE20200226|oclc=	8668235349|pmid=32684529|pmc=7429147|access-date=May 27, 2021|archive-url=https://archive.today/20201113064420/https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC7429147/|archive-date=November 13, 2020|url-status=live}}</ref>
